findings.remediation: Make the dry-run diff safe by construction rather than by key-name recognition. Preferred: redact any changed-line string value that looks credential-shaped (high entropy, long tokens, scheme-less bearer/PAT patterns) with a bounded <redacted> marker, in addition to the existing key-name and URL rules. Alternative or additionally: render the diff from a semantic key-path comparison (only board-owned keys and their immediate parents are shown as +/- lines) or serialize format-preserving so unrelated lines never enter the changed set. Fix the misleading diff header (install.ts:446) to describe actual coverage. Tests: compact single-line config holding {"keep":true,"openai_key":"sk-test-..."} must not print the marker; pretty-printed config with the secret as the final key must not print it; denylisted keys and the six URL-userinfo encodings keep redacting; dry-run still writes nothing.

rootCause.summary: Redaction is keyed to value location (key names, URL userinfo) rather than to the fact that arbitrary pre-existing config lines enter the changed-lines set. Because planJson re-serializes the whole document, changed lines routinely include unrelated keys, and any secret under a key outside the denylist passes through unredacted to stdout. The invariant claimed by backlog 117 #8 (never echo credentials into diffs) needs value-shape-based or format-preserving protection, not a key-name fragment list.

severity.changeConditions: Raise to medium if secrets are shown to routinely sit under non-denylisted keys in affected configs and dry-run output is routinely captured into widely-shared or attacker-readable surfaces, or with a demonstrated in-scope chain steering dry-run execution and observing the transcript. Raise toward high only if untrusted-store content can flow into echoed diff lines (no evidence today). Lower to informational if affected configs provably hold no credentials or a policy explicitly accepts the echo (backlog 117 #8 says the opposite).
severity.rationale: Impact medium: real developer credentials can reach durable capture surfaces (CI logs, agent transcripts, pastes into shared boards), the exact threat-model risk 5. Likelihood low: the secret must sit under a non-denylisted key on a changed line and the operator must run a captured dry-run; no attacker input is required or involved. Matrix medium x low -> low; robust under high x low.

findings.summary: `board install <runtime> --dry-run` prints a unified diff of proposed config changes, and `planJson` re-serializes the whole config so pre-existing lines commonly count as changed (compact single-line configs reflow entirely; pretty-printed files rewrite the former last key's line with a trailing comma). The only redaction on those lines is `safeDiffLine`: a key-name denylist (token|secret|password|credential|private_key|access_key|api_key|authorization) plus URL-userinfo scrubbing. A secret stored under any other key name (for example `openai_key`) is emitted verbatim to stdout inside the diff, violating the backlog 117 #8 claim that the installer never echoes credentials into diffs. Reproduced end-to-end through the real CLI stdout with an invented marker secret; the denylisted-key negative control is correctly redacted.
findings.title: Dry-run config diff redacts only key-name-denylist and URL-userinfo patterns, echoing secrets under other key names to stdout

preventiveControls: Adopt a scan policy for untrusted-store readers: paginate to completion, or bound with an operator-visible truncation signal — never silently stop (applies to board who as well, same cap, pre-existing sibling)
Backlog 305 rate limits / audit view and a presence GC prevent cheap persistent floods; presence signing (301+) complements but does not replace window-bounding
findings.remediation: Bound the read at the in-scope call site and make degradation visible. Preferred: pass an explicit limit (up to MAX_WHO_LIMIT 1000) sized to the deployment, and/or paginate (presence supports an after cursor) until every mentioned agent name has been examined or the store is exhausted. Additionally emit an operator-visible truncation/crowding warning when the window saturates before all mentioned names were seen (deliverOpenCodeMentions or watch shutdown). Longer term (backlog-adjacent): per-author presence rate limits and GC (305), and presence signing (301+) which also fixes the spoofing class but not this window starvation. Tests: flood of 200 records under a low-sorting name then assert the victim is still woken (or a warning is printed); junk keys filling the window; same-name zero-time-ULID crowding variant.

rootCause.summary: The new wake path consumes an untrusted shared store through a bounded reader window (first 200 lexicographic keys) without either bounding to completion or signaling truncation. Presence is unsigned and attacker-writable by design, and nothing rates-limits or garbage-collects presence keys, so window crowding is cheap, persistent, and silent. The general defect class is any reader over the untrusted store that neither paginates to completion nor surfaces an operator-visible truncation.

severity.changeConditions: Raise to medium if wake delivery is shown to carry security-critical function (incident/revocation notices via mentions), if the capped scan ever feeds an integrity or confidentiality decision, or with fleet-scale/default-on evidence. Lower to informational if --deliver stays off by default everywhere and a truncation warning ships (silent starvation becomes detectable degradation). Post-fix: re-run validation_artifacts/flood_poc_e2e.ts expecting delivery or a visible warning.
severity.rationale: Impact medium (availability-only): an in-scope baseline attacker (any store writer) silently and persistently suppresses the new delivery feature for all watchers of a store, with a genuinely silent failure mode. No integrity or confidentiality impact — the endpoint still derives only from the local owner-only registry. Likelihood medium: trivial cost (200 cheap persistent writes, attacker-chosen sort prefix, attacker-writable trigger post) but requires deliberate targeting of an opt-in deployment for disruption-only payoff. Matrix medium x medium -> low.

findings.summary: deliverOpenCodeMentions (new in this change set) resolves wake targets by calling listPresence without a limit, so it examines at most the first 200 presence keys of the untrusted shared store in lexicographic order (DEFAULT_WHO_LIMIT in committed packages/presence, out of diff scope) and stops. Any store writer can cheaply create 200 structurally valid heartbeat records under a low-sorting name; the victim's record is then never examined and the wake silently never fires (errors are discarded by Promise.allSettled and nothing logs). Validated end-to-end through the real sink: 1 wake POST without flood, 0 POSTs with exactly 200 flood records. Availability-only: wake endpoints still derive solely from the local owner-only session registry, so integrity and confidentiality are unaffected.
findings.title: Wake delivery scans only the first 200 lexicographic presence records, so store-flooded records silently suppress wake targets

counterEvidence: Wake endpoints still derive exclusively from the local owner-only session registry (index.ts:365-368), so flooding cannot redirect or forge delivery — integrity/confidentiality unaffected

Store-owner tampering/withholding is an accepted threat-model risk (risk 4), but this attack requires no tampering — it exploits a reader-side window and would also starve an honest store with >200 legitimately active agents
The hook-injection path is index/Board-based and not presence-capped; impact is confined to wake delivery
